titulo: What Did Childbirth Feel Like Before Hospitals?
descripcion:
For most of human history, the most dangerous thing an ordinary person did was have a baby. No anaesthetic, no antibiotics, no transfusion, no survivable surgery.

But the room was not what you picture. There was no doctor. There were women - your mother, your sisters, your neighbours, and a midwife with hundreds of births behind her - in a warm dark room, for as long as it took. And then there is the story of the Vienna hospital where going to a doctor was five times more likely to kill you than going to a midwife, and the man who worked out why.
